title: Speck builds a new dance hall; band changes
summary: Speck builds a bigger hall, the band moves back and forth, Joe is fired, and a new line-up with Edmund Warden, Johnny Thomas and Albert Jackson forms.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So, well, after that, well, he, the white, it looked like it was better for the white, see. So, what he did, he took down some of the petition in the place, you see. Uh-huh. Well, Vinny's begin to pick, really pick up good then, you see. Uh-huh. So, he said, well, I guess I need another, I need a dance hall now. So, this fella, the place was belongs for, he was Italian, you see. Well, he didn't have the money to build the dance hall, you see. So, the fella crossed the street, crossed the street, he have a military there, you see. So, he told the spectre, he said, well, if that fella want to build a dance hall for you, he said, I'll build it for you on the right hand side of the highway, on that side, you see. So, well, everyone, the fella decided, spectre got the money, and, uh, built the place, you see. So, after spectre built the place, we played there, we played for spectre, we opened the place and everything. So, after that, we left from spectre and we went back to Racelet, played for Dutton Lebar, you see. Played for him, went back there and played for the people out there. So, well, that made Elton, see, me and Elton was playing together. So, what we did, me and Joe got out of the band, see. See, he wanted to get rid of Joe, you see, fired Joe. Who did?
When you went back to Racelet, you had Elton, Joe? No, no, I had Joe. Yeah.
Just the two of you? No, no, not two of us.
We just all had a new band, you see. Oh, well, how many people did that?
Edmund Warden, we had Edmund Warden. And, you had an Altar track? Yeah, Edmund Warden. I had a boy called Johnny Thomas, played drum. And had Albert playing trombone.
No, he don't play anymore now.
What's he do now? Does he play anymore?
Albert Jackson. No, he don't play anymore now.
